title: BST Duplicate Detection

description.intro:
A binary search tree (BST) is a binary tree where, for every node:

All the values on its left subtree are less than or equal to the node's value.
All the values on its right subtree are greater than or equal to the node's value.
Given the root of a binary search tree, determine if it contains any duplicate values.

Example:
              5
            /    \
           2      9
            \    / \
             4  9   11
                 \
                  9
Output: True
constraints: The number of nodes is at most 10^5
The height of the tree is at most 500
The value at each node is between 0 and 10^9
description.approach:
The first question we should ask for binary tree problems is: "What information do I need to pass through the tree, and in which direction?"

Information directions
![alt text](image-21.png)

We can follow two approaches:

Pass subtree maximums and minimums up the tree. There is a duplicate if, for some node, node == max(left subtree) or node == min(right subtree).
Do an inorder traversal, and check if two consecutive values are the same. We can store the previous value in the traversal as "global" state, so that we can compare it with the current value.

complexity:
Time & Space Analysis
n: the number of nodes in the tree

h: the height of the tree

Time: O(n) - we visit each node once

Extra space: O(h) - for the call stack

tests.python:
def run_tests():
  # Example 1 - BST with duplicates
  root1 = Node(5,
               Node(2,
                    None,
                    Node(4)),
               Node(9,
                    Node(9,
                         None,
                         Node(9)),
                    Node(11)))

  # Example 2 - empty tree
  root2 = None

  # Example 3 - single node
  root3 = Node(1)

  # Example 4 - BST without duplicates
  root4 = Node(5,
               Node(2,
                    Node(1),
                    Node(4)),
               Node(8,
                    Node(6),
                    Node(9)))

  tests = [
      (root1, True),  # Has duplicates (9s)
      (root4, False),  # No duplicates
  ]

  for i, (root, want) in enumerate(tests):
    got = has_duplicate(root)
    assert got == want, f"\nhas_duplicate(root{        i + 1}): got: {got}, want: {want}\n"

run_tests()
